name: Water-Cooled Turn
description: Unveiled in 1997 and built from 1998, the 996 was the first series 911 with water cooling: tightening emissions rules demanded a four-valve cylinder head that only liquid cooling could keep reliable, and in doing so Porsche extracted 300 PS from the basic 3.4-litre flat-six. Designed by Pinky Lai under chief designer Harm Lagaay, the body was 18.5 cm longer and 3 cm wider than the 993 yet around 50 kg lighter, and it shared its front end and much of its structure with the 986 Boxster — a parts-sharing strategy that critics seized on when they mocked the shared headlight shape. A 2002 facelift brought 3.6-litre power, Turbo-derived styling and the Targa's powered glass roof, while the range ran from the Carrera all the way to the 483 PS GT2. Porsche built 175,262 examples between 1998 and 2005.

variants.name: 911 Carrera
variants.engine: 3.4 L M96 flat-six (to 2001); 3.6 L M96 flat-six (2002–2005)
variants.torque: 350 Nm (258 lb-ft) at 4,600 rpm; 370 Nm (273 lb-ft) at 4,250 rpm from 2002
variants.description: The launch car of the water-cooled era: a 3.4-litre flat-six with four valves per cylinder, 300 PS and a 0–100 km/h sprint of 5.2 seconds in a body roughly 50 kg lighter than the 993 it replaced. It arrived as a coupé and cabriolet, rear-wheel drive, with either a six-speed manual or five-speed Tiptronic S. The 2002 facelift raised capacity to 3.6 litres and output to 320 PS, sharpened the front end with Turbo-derived lights, and rewrote the numbers: 4.9 seconds to 100 km/h and 286 km/h flat out.

variants.name: 911 Carrera S
variants.description: There has never been a 996-generation 911 Carrera S. Porsche dropped the S suffix after the 993, and the 996 range runs from the Carrera through the all-wheel-drive Carrera 4S — a model introduced in 2002 that plays the part a buyer might expect a Carrera S to fill. The badge returned on the 997 in 2005. This roster entry is retained so the variant id survives across generations, but no 996 specifications can honestly be attached to it.

variants.name: 911 Carrera 4
variants.torque: 350 Nm (258 lb-ft) at 4,600 rpm; 370 Nm (273 lb-ft) at 4,250 rpm from 2002
variants.weight: 1,375 kg (3,032 lb) coupé 3.4 L; 1,483 kg (3,267 lb) cabriolet 3.6 L
variants.description: From October 1998 the 996 range gained permanent all-wheel drive, a system that sent between five and forty percent of torque to the front wheels as conditions demanded. The Carrera 4 was the accessible way into four-wheel-drive 911 traction, sharing the 3.4-litre 300 PS engine with the rear-drive Carrera and taking on the 320 PS 3.6-litre when the cabriolet was updated for 2002. The narrow-body coupé ended its run in 2001, making way for the wide-bodied Carrera 4S, while the Carrera 4 Cabriolet — with its Z-fold roof and removable hardtop — continued until 2004.
missing: Carrera 4 (3.4 L) top speed differs by source: Wikipedia EU-spec lists 274 km/h, Excellence lists 174 mph (280 km/h). Wikipedia figure used.

variants.name: 911 Carrera 4S
variants.description: The 4S gave the 996 a second, more aggressive shape: the Turbo's wide 1,830 mm body, its wheels and its brakes, but with the 3.6-litre naturally aspirated engine in place of the twin-turbo. Launched for 2002 as a coupé — the cabriolet followed for 2004 — it combined permanent all-wheel drive with 320 PS, 370 Nm, a 5.1-second sprint to 100 km/h and a 280 km/h top speed. Wider rear arches, cross-drilled discs and the aero-tuned front end made it the most planted naturally aspirated 996, and today it is among the generation's most sought-after variants.

sources.title: How to buy a Porsche 996 — Porsche

variants.name: 911 Targa
variants.description: Available from December 2001, the 996 Targa replaced the old lift-off roof panel with an electrically operated glass surface of more than 16 square feet (roughly 1.5 m²) — the largest glass area ever fitted to a 911 — and, for the first time, a rear window that powered upwards. Unusually for a 996 badged Targa, it was rear-wheel drive; the Targa 4 and Targa 4S names only arrived with the 997. The 3.6-litre 320 PS flat-six and six-speed manual gave 0–100 km/h in 5.2 seconds and 285 km/h, at a 1,415 kg kerb weight.

variants.name: 911 Turbo
variants.description: Launched in spring 2000 with VINs assigned to model year 2001, the 996 Turbo used the GT2's 3.6-litre twin-turbo flat-six in road-trimmed form: 420 PS and 563 Nm, routed through all-wheel drive into a 1,540 kg coupé. It reached 100 km/h in 4.2 seconds and ran to 304 km/h, with ceramic composite brakes optional and 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels under Turbo-look bodywork fed by its side intakes. A Cabriolet followed, and the run closed with the 450 PS Turbo S.

variants.name: 911 Turbo S
variants.description: The final and most potent 996 Turbo: 450 PS and 620 Nm from the twin-turbo 3.6, with ceramic composite brakes and six-piston front calipers as standard equipment plus Turbo S badging and a revised rear deck. Offered only for the 2004 and 2005 model years, it weighed 1,590 kg in manual form and, on Excellence's figures, matched the regular Turbo's 4.2-second 0–100 km/h while lifting top speed to 306 km/h. Coupé and cabriolet were both built; other sources quote a quicker 3.9-second sprint, so the conflict is recorded in missing.
missing: Turbo S performance figures conflict between sources: Excellence lists 4.2 s (0–100 km/h) and 190 mph (306 km/h) for the manual coupé, while Wikipedia quotes 3.9 s and 317 km/h. Excellence figures used.

variants.name: 911 GT3
variants.engine: 3.6 L naturally aspirated flat-6 (11.7:1 compression, 8,200 rpm max)
variants.torque: 370 Nm (273 lb-ft) to 2001; 385 Nm (284 lb-ft) from 2002
variants.topSpeed: 302 km/h (188 mph) Mk1; 306 km/h (190 mph) Mk2
variants.description: Porsche's first GT3 arrived in May 1999 as a homologation special built on the stiffer Carrera 4 bodyshell: a high-revving naturally aspirated 3.6 flat-six with 11.7:1 compression and 8,200 rpm available, no rear seats, bucket seats, firmer adjustable suspension and cross-drilled brakes. The Mk1 made 360 PS and covered 0–100 km/h in 4.8 seconds at 1,350 kg; the 2002 Mk2 lifted output to 381 PS and torque to 385 Nm, cut the sprint to 4.5 seconds and ran to 306 km/h. Rear-wheel drive and a six-speed manual kept it the purest 996 on track.

variants.name: 911 GT3 RS
variants.description: The 996 GT3 RS was the lightest and most focused normally aspirated 996: the Mk2 GT3's 381 PS flat-six and six-speed manual in a body trimmed to 1,360 kg through thinner glass, lightweight composites and the deletion of rear seats. It carried red-accented graphics, lightweight bucket seats and 18-inch forged wheels, reached 100 km/h in 4.4 seconds and topped out at 306 km/h. Built in 682 examples across the 2003 and 2004 model years, coupé only, it revived the RS name for the first time since the air-cooled era.

sources.title: Porsche 911 Coupe (996 series) GT3 RS specs — Ultimate Specs

variants.name: 911 GT2
variants.description: The GT2 took the 996 Turbo's drivetrain and removed everything Porsche could live without: all-wheel drive, rear seats and around 100 kg of mass. It ran with 462 PS in 2001–2002 form and 483 PS from 2003, driving the rear wheels through a six-speed manual with ceramic composite brakes standard, 315-section rear tyres and 1,440 kg to haul. It cracked 100 km/h in 4.0 seconds and ran to 314 km/h — the fastest production 911 of its day. Homologated for GT2-class racing, it was rawer and far rarer than the Turbo, and famously unforgiving of mistakes.

variants.name: 911 America Roadster
variants.description: No 996 America Roadster was ever built. The name belongs two generations earlier: Porsche's 964 911 America Roadster of 1992 and 1993, a Turbo-bodied, Turbo-sprung cabriolet made for the North American market in a run of exactly 250 cars, echoing the 356 America Roadster. The 996 range contains no such model — its open cars are the Carrera Cabriolet, Carrera 4 Cabriolet, Carrera 4S Cabriolet and Turbo Cabriolet. This entry exists only because the roster carries the id across generations; every specification field is intentionally null.

variants.name: 911 Millennium Edition
variants.description: For the turn of the millennium Porsche dressed a Carrera 4 in Violet Chromaflair — a paint that shifts from deep violet towards green as the light changes — over natural caramel leather with dark burr maple trim and chrome 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels. A numbered console plate and a '911' badge on the engine lid marked each car out. Just 911 examples were built for model year 2000, each with the 300 PS 3.4-litre flat-six and permanent all-wheel drive, in six-speed manual or Tiptronic form: a collector's specification rather than a performance statement.
missing: Millennium Edition kerb weight not found in any source consulted; no 0–100 km/h figure is quoted either (source gives 0–60 mph 5.2 s only), so acceleration is stated in imperial.

variants.name: 911 40th Anniversary (40 Jahre)
variants.engine: 3.6 L flat-6 with X51 power kit
variants.description: Built to mark 40 years of the 911, the 40th Anniversary (40 Jahre 911) was a rear-drive Carrera coupé given the X51 power kit as standard: 254 kW (345 PS) instead of 320, via new camshafts and exhaust manifolds rather than a simple remap. It also gained a limited-slip differential, lowered sports suspension, a Turbo front bumper, 18-inch Carrera II wheels, dark grey leather sports seats with a numbered plaque and, exclusively, GT Silver Metallic paint. Porsche made 1,963 of them for model year 2004 — one for every year since the 911 arrived in 1963.
missing: 40th Anniversary: no verified 0–100 km/h or top-speed figure found in any source consulted, so both fields are null. Curb weight (1,370 kg) rests on a single source (Carfolio).
